text:
Kiefer Sherwood is the undrafted, hard-hitting winger who scored 23 goals for Vancouver last season, and San Jose brought him in to be exactly that. Twenty games in, the effort is there and the goals aren't: two, on 36 shots, a 5.6% shooting rate against a normal range of about 10 to 15%.

That looks like bad luck more than decline. His 3.45 expected goals (the quality of his chances) say he's about a goal and a half short, and he has a 94th-percentile shot. He's found other ways to contribute, with seven assists and six points in his last ten while his ice time has climbed to about 16:38 a night. Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.6 wins above replacement last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says 52% of his shots come off the rush. He's also become a voice: after the 6-2 loss in Los Angeles, Sportskeeda reported him calling out the Kings for "disrespectful" antics. On a rebuilding team that's losing a lot, a veteran who cares that much is worth something. The goals should follow.
